items.statement: In consecutive patients booked for major abdominal surgery, a 30-second sit-to-stand count of 10 or fewer detects an anaerobic threshold below 11 mL/kg/min (or inability to complete exercise testing) with sensitivity of at least 75 percent.
items.rationale: Triage needs high sensitivity so that unfit patients are not missed; 75 percent is the lower bound the triage group judged acceptable; the published estimate is 78 percent with an optimistic cut-off (c1).
items.risks: Blinding lapses; CPET capacity; prevalence lower than planned.

items.statement: Adding gait speed below 1.0 m/s to the sit-to-stand test raises sensitivity without an unacceptable fall in specificity.
items.rationale: A combination rule is used elsewhere without accuracy data.

items.statement: Bedside triage would let most prioritised patients start prehabilitation at least four weeks before surgery.
items.rationale: Waiting for testing delayed almost half elsewhere (c6).
items.risks: Not tested in this study; follows only if accuracy is adequate.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 is the primary validation target.
